title_candidates: Hugging Face makes more models fast in vLLM without custom ports
summary: Hugging Face says the transformers backend for vLLM now reaches native-speed inference for many architectures, making new model serving easier for teams using open models.

primary_source.title: Native-speed vLLM transformers modeling backend
primary_source.author: Hugging Face
key_facts: Hugging Face says the transformers modeling backend for vLLM is now as fast or faster than custom vLLM implementations for many LLM architectures.
The update lets model authors use transformers implementations for fast vLLM inference without writing a separate custom vLLM model implementation.
Hugging Face tested three Qwen3 models, including dense and mixture-of-experts cases.
The feature can be selected with the model implementation option for compatible models.
Models using linear attention and custom code living only in a Hub repo may not work yet.

prerequisites: A machine or cloud runtime that can run vLLM

steps.instruction: Pick a small public model you already know how to serve, such as a small Qwen model.
Check the vLLM supported-models page before spending GPU time.
Run the model once with your current serving path and save simple latency notes.
Try the transformers backend option on the same prompt set and compare whether quality and speed stay acceptable.
Do not switch production traffic until you have tested your exact model, context length, tools, and hardware.

risk_flags: Developer-leaning article; kept because it materially lowers open-model serving friction.
